Cautiously positive. The statement highlights solid job gains and firmer business investment while acknowledging a temporary growth slowdown and inflation still somewhat below the 2 percent goal. That mix aligns with the natural-rate perspective of Friedman and Phelps, which cautions against overinterpreting low unemployment as a mandate to tighten given no long-run inflation-unemployment trade-off. The Committee’s emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent objective and inflation expectations is consistent with Svensson’s flexible inflation-forecast targeting, supporting patience when core inflation softens. The commitment to gradual, data-dependent rate increases accords with interest-rate rule guidance in McCallum and Nelson (1999), while maintaining accommodation avoids the consumption growth headwinds often associated with premature tightening (Canzoneri, Cumby, and Diba, 2007). Continued monitoring of financial and international developments is also consistent with literature on financial frictions and the accelerator, justifying a balanced tone.
